name: How often should siding caulk be inspected or replaced?

mainEntity.name: How often should siding caulk be inspected or replaced?

acceptedAnswer.text: Siding caulk should typically be inspected annually, ideally in spring or fall, to identify any signs of cracking, shrinking, or detachment. For replacement, the lifespan of caulk varies significantly based on the type used, sun exposure, and weather conditions. High-quality elastomeric caulks can last 10-20 years, while cheaper acrylic latex caulks may need replacement every 3-5 years. In the Bay Area, fluctuating temperatures and coastal humidity can accelerate wear, so regular inspection is crucial to maintain an effective seal.
acceptedAnswer.description: Inspect siding caulk annually for damage. Replacement frequency varies by caulk type, lasting from 3-5 years for basic caulk up to 10-20 years for high-quality elastomeric products.
